_about: People-centred reading of each visible change in the 3D future scene. 'gains' and 'costs' name who could benefit and who could bear the costs; 'question' is the right-to-the-city question it raises. Interpretations, not findings. The numbers shown alongside come from the forecasts.

corridor.title: Highway corridor grows
corridor.gains: Office, mall and hotel jobs (guards, cleaners, drivers, delivery riders); landowners near the highway
corridor.costs: Street vendors moved off widened footpaths; renters facing rising rents; older shops priced out
corridor.question: Who captures the value of the highway: long-time residents and traders, or new developers?

redevelop.title: Old plots rebuilt
redevelop.gains: Owners who sell or rebuild; construction workers (often migrant, often short-term)
redevelop.costs: Tenants of older houses, home-based workers who lose ground-floor space, and neighbours living with dust and noise
redevelop.question: Does redevelopment include affordable homes for people already living here?

densify.title: Neighbourhoods fill up
densify.gains: More people within walking distance of shops and buses; more customers for local trade
densify.costs: Pressure on water, drains, schools and the little open space left; smaller homes for families
densify.question: Do services and public space grow as fast as the number of people?

solar.title: Solar on rooftops
solar.gains: Owners who control their roofs get lower bills; local installers and electricians find new work
solar.costs: Tenants and informal settlements rarely benefit; upfront costs exclude poorer households
solar.question: Can the green transition reach renters and the poor, through shared or community solar?

haze.title: Air quality
haze.gains: If air gets cleaner, everyone who lives and works outdoors breathes easier
haze.costs: If it gets worse, street vendors, auto drivers, traffic police and children by the highway are hit hardest
haze.question: Clean air is shared unequally: who gets protected first?

traffic.title: Busier highway
traffic.gains: Auto and taxi drivers, delivery riders and roadside businesses see more customers
traffic.costs: Pedestrians, cyclists and children face more danger and longer, hotter waits to cross
traffic.question: Is road space shared fairly between cars and the many people who walk, cycle or take the bus?

heat.title: Summer heat
heat.gains: If very hot days become rarer, outdoor work and travel get safer
heat.costs: If they become common, vendors, construction workers, delivery riders and older people in tin-roofed homes lose income and health
heat.question: Shade, drinking water and cooling centres decide who can safely use the city in summer.
